label: Bhajana-Lālasā Song Four
title: dāna, pratigraha, mitho gupta-kathā
metaDescription: Bhajana-Lālasā Song Four (dāna, pratigraha, mitho gupta-kathā,) of Śaraṇāgati (‘Surrender’) written by Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in 1893. This songbook contains 50 songs detailing the six symptoms of surrender unto the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

verses.translation: O my Lord Hari! Offering and receiving gifts, giving and receiving spiritual food, revealing one’s thoughts, and making confidential inquiries-these are the six characteristics of loving association, and in them is found the very life of devotion. *

translit: tattva nā bujhiye, jñāne vā ajñāne,
verses.translation: I have failed to understand the truth, and by practicing these six activities with non-devotees, either knowingly or unknowingly, I lost all devotional inclination and have become a materialist. Consequently You, O Lord, still remain far away.
deva: तत्त्व ना बुझिये, ज्ञाने वा अज्ञाने,
bengali: তত্ত্ব না বুঝিযে, জ্ঞানে বা অজ্ঞানে,

verses.translation: The day I cherish these activities of intimate association with the devotees of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, that very day the high goddess of devotion will take her seat upon the throne of my heart.

When will I give up the company of those who are addicted to the company of materialistic women and those who are averse to You? And when will I cultivate the constant association of Your devotees, O Lord?
